Consider the two curves defined algebraically and graphed below.

\[y=2+\sqrt{12x-36}\] \[y=2x-3\]


The horizontal coordinates of the intersections, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\), are also the solutions to the equation below:

\[2+\sqrt{12x-36}=2x-3\]

Solve that equation.

\[2+\sqrt{12x-36}=2x-3\]

Subtract 2 from both sides.

\[\sqrt{12x-36}=2x-5\]

Square both sides.\[12x-36=(2x-5)^2\]

Expand the right side.\[12x-36=4x^2-20x+25\]

Subtract \(12x-36\) from both sides.\[0=4x^2-32x+61\]

Use the quadratic formula.

\[x=\frac{-(-32)\pm\sqrt{(-32)^2-4(4)(61)}}{2(4)}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{32\pm\sqrt{1024-976}}{8}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{32\pm\sqrt{48}}{8}\]

Simplify the radical.\[x=\frac{32\pm4\sqrt{3}}{8}\]

Simplify based on common factor of 4.

\[x=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{3}}{2}\]

Consider the two curves defined algebraically and graphed below.

\[y=6+\sqrt{14x-70}\] \[y=3x-8\]


The horizontal coordinates of the intersections, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\), are also the solutions to the equation below:

\[6+\sqrt{14x-70}=3x-8\]

Solve that equation.

\[6+\sqrt{14x-70}=3x-8\]

Subtract 6 from both sides.

\[\sqrt{14x-70}=3x-14\]

Square both sides.\[14x-70=(3x-14)^2\]

Expand the right side.\[14x-70=9x^2-84x+196\]

Subtract \(14x-70\) from both sides.\[0=9x^2-98x+266\]

Use the quadratic formula.

\[x=\frac{-(-98)\pm\sqrt{(-98)^2-4(9)(266)}}{2(9)}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{98\pm\sqrt{9604-9576}}{18}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{98\pm\sqrt{28}}{18}\]

Simplify the radical.\[x=\frac{98\pm2\sqrt{7}}{18}\]

Simplify based on common factor of 2.

\[x=\frac{49\pm\sqrt{7}}{9}\]

Consider the two curves defined algebraically and graphed below.

\[y=5+\sqrt{9x-54}\] \[y=2x-6\]


The horizontal coordinates of the intersections, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\), are also the solutions to the equation below:

\[5+\sqrt{9x-54}=2x-6\]

Solve that equation.

\[5+\sqrt{9x-54}=2x-6\]

Subtract 5 from both sides.

\[\sqrt{9x-54}=2x-11\]

Square both sides.\[9x-54=(2x-11)^2\]

Expand the right side.\[9x-54=4x^2-44x+121\]

Subtract \(9x-54\) from both sides.\[0=4x^2-53x+175\]

Use the quadratic formula.

\[x=\frac{-(-53)\pm\sqrt{(-53)^2-4(4)(175)}}{2(4)}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{53\pm\sqrt{2809-2800}}{8}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{53\pm\sqrt{9}}{8}\]

Simplify the radical.\[x=\frac{53\pm3}{8}\]

Consider the two curves defined algebraically and graphed below.

\[y=-2+\sqrt{11x+44}\] \[y=2x+7\]


The horizontal coordinates of the intersections, \(x_1\) and \(x_2\), are also the solutions to the equation below:

\[-2+\sqrt{11x+44}=2x+7\]

Solve that equation.

\[-2+\sqrt{11x+44}=2x+7\]

Add 2 to both sides.

\[\sqrt{11x+44}=2x+9\]

Square both sides.\[11x+44=(2x+9)^2\]

Expand the right side.\[11x+44=4x^2+36x+81\]

Subtract \(11x+44\) from both sides.\[0=4x^2+25x+37\]

Use the quadratic formula.

\[x=\frac{-(25)\pm\sqrt{(25)^2-4(4)(37)}}{2(4)}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{-25\pm\sqrt{625-592}}{8}\]

Simplify.\[x=\frac{-25\pm\sqrt{33}}{8}\]

The discriminant, 33, has no perfect-square factors, so we are done simplifying.
